paragraphs: R’ Yose son of R’ Tanchum of Kefar Aggin.

Hyman cites Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 2:6 for the story: “(a man whose neighbor) Acha wished to set sail (to sea) between the Festival and Chanukah. His father appeared to him (and said), ‘He had no burial either.’ He heeded neither warning.” The supplied introduction is difficult. Hyman also cites the parallel in Bereshit Rabbah and Kohelet Rabbah with R’ Yehoshua son of R’ Tanchuma of Kefar Chanun [supplied locators פ״דה and פ״כב].
And in the Yalkut on Isaiah, remez 317 (printed שיז), the reading is R’ Yehoshua son of R’ Tanchum bar Chiya.

notes.text: The supplied neighbor/Acha construction remains unclear. The checked Shabbat text has אתא, “came,” rather than a man called Acha, and includes a woman’s warning before the father’s appearance. Hyman’s parallel Yehoshua/Yose and patronymic/place variants remain distinct.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier Shabbat comparison has אתא, came, beside supplied אחא; this does not prove a tav/chet transcription history or license categorical removal of Acha from this supplied text. The parenthetical neighbor introduction remains difficult. Hyman’s sea/Festival-to-Chanukah/father/burial/negation narrative remains complete; the earlier parallel includes an additional woman’s warning which is not imported. Supplied פ״דה and פ״כב remain literal rather than guessed chapters. Kefar Chanun editorial provenance and user-adjudicated remez317 are retained. Yose/Yehoshua and Tanchum/Tanchuma/barChiyya alternatives are not merged; titles stay R-prime.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud names Yose son of Tanchum of Kefar Aggin, in Essia, with אתא and the matron’s warning before the appearance of his father. Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 737) has the parenthetical introduction, אחא and “and he said to him.” In the consulted Jerusalem Talmud, the burial words follow the father’s appearance without that speech formula. Bereshit Rabbah 6:5 and Kohelet Rabbah 3:2 both give the father’s burial warning as speech in a dream. Both name Yehoshua, but Bereshit Rabbah gives Tanchuma son of Chiyya of Kefar Chanun and Kohelet Rabbah gives Tanchum son of Chiyya of Kefar Agon. The consulted Yalkut has Yehoshua son of Tanchum son of Rabbi Chiyya at remez 455. The translation retains the supplied 317. The parallel accounts do not establish that the names or places are interchangeable.
